Selected Work

McDonald’s Equity Research & Valuation

Fundamental Valuation · Bloomberg Technical Analysis · Investment Research

A multi-method equity valuation and Bloomberg technical analysis of McDonald’s Corporation, combining long-term fundamental value with near-term market signals to support a HOLD recommendation.

Prepared by Alexander Jenkins

Project Overview

I evaluated McDonald’s using multiple fundamental valuation methodologies and technical indicators to determine whether the company’s market price was supported by its underlying value.

The analysis used several valuation methods to estimate McDonald’s intrinsic value, then compared those results with technical indicators from Bloomberg Terminal. This allowed me to identify where fundamental and technical signals supported or contradicted one another and use those findings to form an overall investment recommendation.

Company
McDonald’s Corporation (NYSE: MCD)
Analysis Period
March 19–22, 2026
Market Price
$308.85
Final Recommendation
HOLD

Tools & Methods

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Bloomberg Terminal
  • Morningstar
  • SEC EDGAR
  • CAPM
  • Dividend Discount Models
  • Free Cash Flow
  • Residual Income
  • Relative Valuation

Valuation Analysis

Comparing Multiple Approaches

Rather than relying on a single valuation methodology, I analyzed McDonald’s using several approaches to understand how different assumptions affected implied equity value.

Valuation Method Implied Value
Constant Growth DDM $225.64
Non-Constant Growth DDM $230.94
H-Model $281.54
Free Cash Flow $430.66
Residual Income $364.65
P/E $335.94
P/Sales $325.49
P/Cash Flow $346.19

The valuation methods produced a wide range of implied values. Dividend-based approaches generally suggested a valuation below market price, while free cash flow, residual income, and relative valuation methods indicated potential upside.

This dispersion reinforced the importance of understanding the assumptions and sensitivities underlying each valuation model rather than relying on a single calculated price.

Technical Analysis

I used Bloomberg Terminal to supplement the fundamental analysis with an evaluation of McDonald’s historical price behavior and technical indicators.

The Review Included

  • Head-and-shoulders patterns
  • Price-channel analysis
  • 50, 100, and 200-day moving averages
  • Bollinger Bands
  • Fibonacci retracement levels

Most of the technical indicators reflected bearish near-term momentum. At the same time, Fibonacci analysis showed the stock approaching an important support level, creating a more mixed technical picture.

Key Assumptions

Valuation assumptions included McDonald’s historical growth, a market-based required return calculated using CAPM, and a long-term growth assumption.

Because McDonald’s had negative shareholders’ equity, I did not rely on the sustainable growth rate as a meaningful input. I instead evaluated historical growth and used a more conservative long-term growth assumption.

The analysis also considered how changes in growth and required return assumptions could materially affect calculated intrinsic value.

Investment Conclusion

Final Recommendation HOLD

Market price at analysis: $308.85

The fundamental and technical analyses produced conflicting signals.

Several fundamental valuation methods, including free cash flow, residual income, and relative valuation, produced implied values above McDonald’s $308.85 market price and suggested potential upside. Dividend-based models produced more conservative estimates below the market price.

Technical analysis was generally more bearish, with price-channel behavior, moving averages, Bollinger Bands, and other indicators suggesting weaker near-term momentum.

Given the divergence between longer-term fundamental value and shorter-term technical conditions, I concluded that a HOLD recommendation was the most appropriate at the time of analysis.
